summary: This is a SaaS marketing landing page for Lumen, an analytics platform that turns raw product telemetry into automated reports, alerts, and shared team dashboards.

stack.name: Next.js (App Router)
stack.why: Provides React SSR/SSG for optimal SEO, fast load times, and built-in API route handling.

stack.name: Tailwind CSS
stack.why: Rapid utility-first styling to accurately match exact spacing, gradient treatments, and responsive rules.

stack.name: Supabase (PostgreSQL)
stack.why: Free tier managed PostgreSQL database for waitlists, demo booking requests, and auth.

stack.name: NextAuth.js / Supabase Auth
stack.why: Handles user authentication and session cookies for the Sign In flow.

stack.name: Vercel
stack.why: Seamless zero-configuration hosting and instant edge deployments for Next.js.

components.name: Navbar
components.purpose: Displays company logo, primary navigation links (Product, Pricing, Docs, Blog), and the Sign In outline button.

components.name: Hero
components.purpose: Renders marketing headline, subtext, call-to-action buttons, and the purple preview placeholder container.

components.name: FeatureCard
components.purpose: Renders an individual feature block showing a bold title and a muted explanatory paragraph inside a card surface.

components.name: FeatureGrid
components.purpose: Lays out the feature cards in a responsive three-column grid below the hero section.

components.name: DemoModal
components.purpose: Modal dialog that opens when 'Book a demo →' is clicked to collect visitor email and organization details.

behaviour: Sign in button: Navigates to `/login` or opens auth authentication modal.
Start free trial button: Routes directly to sign-up onboarding funnel `/signup`.
Book a demo link: Opens modal to capture lead information (email, company size, name).
Nav links: Scroll to corresponding sections (#product, #pricing) or navigate to documentation and blog directories.
data: Demo lead payload: email (string), full_name (optional string), created_at (timestamp)

backend.summary: Lightweight Next.js Route Handlers connect to Supabase PostgreSQL to record demo bookings and manage newsletter/waitlist leads.
backend.database: Supabase PostgreSQL for reliable relational persistence and row-level security.
backend.auth: Public landing page does not require active sessions; authentication is delegated via Supabase Auth or NextAuth on `/login`.

tables.name: leads
tables.columns: id uuid default gen_random_uuid() pk, email text not null, full_name text, created_at timestamptz default now()

endpoints.purpose: Stores lead contact information when visitor books a demo

rules: Email field must be well-formed and non-empty.
Rate limit demo requests to max 5 submissions per IP per hour.

pitfalls: Missing mobile layout adaptation: failing to wrap the hero into a single column causes horizontal overflow on screens under 768px.
Incorrect color contrast: using text that is too light instead of measured #797979 fails WCAG AA readability requirements on light gray background.
Unoptimized video/media in placeholder: hero right block will likely host a demo video or heavy graphic; neglecting Next.js image/video optimization will harm Core Web Vitals (LCP).
testing: Unit test FeatureCard to ensure title and description render properly.
E2E test with Playwright verifying 'Book a demo →' link opens lead dialog.
Accessibility test using axe-core to ensure 100% color contrast compliance and focus visibility.
deploy: Push project code to a public or private GitHub repository.
Import repository into Vercel and set required environment variables (SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY).
Deploy on Vercel's global edge network with custom domain configuration.

tokens.method: Colours: pixel quantisation of the whole screenshot and of each detected element. Font sizes: text box height ÷ 1.25. Spacing: gaps between sibling boxes, snapped to a 4px grid. Measured approximations, not values read from source code.
